source_text: Post has ostensiones in carcere etiam diebus paucis commorati, producuntur in publicum, ut eos Cirtensium magistratus elogio fortissimae confessionis honoratos transmitterent cum parte iam damnationis ad praesidem. Et ecce unus e circumstantibus fratribus nostris omnium in se gentilium conuertit oculos, quod iam per gratiam proximae passionis Christus in eius ore et facie relucebat. Cumque ex eo turbulentis et furentibus animis quaereretur an eiusdem et ipse esset religionis et nominis, rapuit tam dulcem promptissima confessione comitatum. Elogiis suis beati martyres plures dei testes, dum ipsi ad martyrium parantur, adquirunt; et iam transmissi ad praesidem, negotiosum ac difficile iter cum uoluntate properabant. Tunc eos praesidi admotos iterum Lambesitanus carcer accepit. Haec enim sola apud gentiles hospitia iustorum.
pass_a_gloss: After these visions, having remained in the prison also for a few days, they are brought forward into public, so that the magistrates of the Cirtensians, having honored them with an official report of most-courageous confession, might forward them with a share of condemnation already to the governor. And behold one from the standing-around brothers of ours turned upon himself the eyes of all the pagans, because already through the grace of the near suffering Christ was shining in his mouth and face. And when it was demanded from him with agitated and raging minds whether he himself also was of the same religion and name, he seized so sweet a companionship with most-ready confession. By their official reports the blessed martyrs gain more witnesses of God, while they themselves are being prepared for martyrdom; and now forwarded to the governor, they hastened the troublesome and difficult journey with willingness. Then the Lambaesitan prison received them when brought before the governor. For these are the only lodgings of the just among the pagans.
pass_b_english: After these visions in prison, they remained there a few days longer and were then led out before the people, so that the magistrates of Cirta might honor them with the formal charge of a most courageous confession and send them on to the governor with part of their sentence already pronounced. And behold, one of the brethren standing around us drew upon himself the eyes of all the heathen, for by the grace of his now approaching suffering Christ was already shining in his mouth and face. When they demanded of him with restless and furious spirits whether he too belonged to the same faith and Name, he seized that sweet fellowship with a most prompt confession.

Thus by their own charges the blessed martyrs win many more witnesses for God even while they themselves are being made ready for martyrdom, and once handed over for the governor they hastened along the burdensome and hard road with willing hearts. Then, when they had been presented to the governor, the prison at Lambaesis received them. For such prisons are the only inns the righteous find among the heathen.
